summary: Deliver a scene as a bounded embed with a versioned command/event API, element-size ownership, origin validation, teardown and semantic fallback.
objective: The same scene can be mounted twice, resized by its containers, controlled through documented messages and removed without cross-instance state or resource leaks.
intent_signals: embed this Three.js scene in another site
example_prompts: Package a product viewer that can be embedded twice on one page.
Define a safe cross-origin command API for a spatial scene iframe.
Make a scene component respond to its own container instead of only window resize.
not_for: Accepting arbitrary code or unvalidated messages from embedding pages.

principles: An embed contract names its surface: mount inputs, commands, events, state snapshot, failure states, fallback and teardown. DOM internals and scene-child indices are private implementation details.
Layout ownership follows the embedding element. Window size is insufficient when panels, grids or multiple embeds resize independently.
Cross-origin messaging is an input boundary. Validate origin, source/instance identity, protocol version, message shape and command authorization before mutating scene state.
implementation: Publish a small versioned protocol: ready/capabilities/state/error events and setView/select/setTime/reset/dispose commands. Include instance ID and request ID so two embeds and asynchronous replies cannot cross.

Observe the actual host element box, update renderer size and camera projection in one scheduled layout step, and disconnect the observer during teardown. Treat zero-size and hidden states explicitly instead of allocating a zero or stale drawing buffer.

For iframe transport, send to an exact configured target origin and accept only expected event.origin plus the registered event.source. Validate the structured payload against the protocol before dispatch; never turn message data into executable code.

Keep Blender asset names as stable semantic IDs only when declared in the export contract. Three.js owns mapping those IDs to scene objects, accessible controls and state events. A non-WebGL fallback exposes the same meaningful state through host-visible markup or another equivalent control surface.
observable_checks: Two embeds with different instance IDs accept only their own commands, keep independent cameras/selections and emit replies to the correct host.
Resizing either container without a window resize updates only that canvas and its camera aspect; repeated hide/show does not accumulate observers or loops.
Messages from a wrong origin, wrong source window, unsupported version, unknown command or invalid payload produce no scene mutation and a bounded diagnostic.
After dispose, the instance emits no events, runs no loop and retains no host listeners; remount creates exactly one fresh instance.

creative_affordances: The host may present the embed as a card, full-bleed panel, comparison cell or narrative step.
Commands may expose domain-specific views while preserving the same envelope and validation rules.
known_limits: Same-origin direct component calls may replace postMessage but still need instance and lifecycle boundaries.
No embed, resize, message, accessibility or disposal behavior was executed.

claims.statement: Resize Observer observes changes to an Element’s size, can observe content-box, border-box or device-pixel-content-box sizes, and provides disconnect to clear observation targets.
claims.scope: CSSWG Resize Observer Level 1 Editor’s Draft read 2026-09-08; browser support and box choice remain target-specific.

claims.statement: The HTML Standard advises postMessage receivers to check event.origin and expected data format, and advises against wildcard targetOrigin for confidential messages.
claims.scope: WHATWG HTML living standard Web Messaging security guidance read 2026-09-08; application authentication and authorization remain separate.
